observations.radius_rule: Multiply SPARC radii by 14.1/13.8 and retain rescaled radii at or below 38.6 kpc.
observations.uncertainty_rule: Use the tabulated SPARC e_Vobs random errors as independent Gaussian standard deviations.

shared_baryonic_input.stellar_geometry: Infinitesimally thin exponential disk with published scale length 4.0 kpc and published fitted stellar disk mass 3.644e10 solar masses at unit scale.
shared_baryonic_input.gas_geometry: Infinitesimally thin exponential disk with scale length four times the stellar scale and 1.4 times the published HI mass.
shared_baryonic_input.stellar_scale_parameter: q_star multiplies the published stellar disk mass and every stellar term; gas terms remain fixed.
shared_baryonic_input.boundary: This common analytic geometry makes the three model families comparable to one another, but it is not the SPARC numerical 3.6-micron baryonic mass model and is not identical to the original heterogeneous blue-band fitting dataset.

models.prediction: Newtonian baryons plus the NFW circular-speed formula with r200=100*V200/H0 kpc.
Published Mannheim--O'Brien stellar/gas Newtonian and linear disk terms plus fixed gamma0 and kappa terms.

fit_objective: Minimize chi-squared=sum(((v_model-v_obs)/e_Vobs)^2) over the declared closed parameter box.

primary_sources.citation: J. F. Navarro, C. S. Frenk, and S. D. M. White, A Universal Density Profile from Hierarchical Clustering, Astrophys. J. 490 (1997) 493
F. Lelli, S. S. McGaugh, and J. M. Schombert, SPARC: Mass Models for 175 Disk Galaxies with Spitzer Photometry and Accurate Rotation Curves, Astron. J. 152 (2016) 157
primary_sources.role: observed rotation curve, random velocity errors, and the distinction between observed-profile SPARC components and the common analytic geometry

primary_sources.citation: P. D. Mannheim and J. G. O'Brien, Fitting galactic rotation curves with conformal gravity and a global quadratic potential, Phys. Rev. D 85 (2012) 124020
primary_sources.role: common exponential baryonic geometry and conformal-gravity prediction

identity of the analytic baryonic geometry with the SPARC numerical mass components or the original Mannheim fitting data
a cosmological concentration--mass prior or a posterior probability for an NFW halo
population-level performance, held-out prediction, or model selection beyond NGC 3198
that the best score in this bounded protocol validates a complete theory or refutes another theory
